C3905.label: stop_line
C3905.reason: The movement happened as described, but it is not a stop_line event. I checked the frames from 104 to 117 s at 0.2 s steps. The white SUV stood with its rear at proxy x≈584, y≈305-340, beside the nose kerb at about (623,278). That puts it entirely past the north_sb crossing, whose bottom edge at that x is y≈279, so it is inside the junction box and not on the crossing or near the stop line. It crept forward from about 105.6 to 107.4-107.6, front moving to about (705,370), stopped behind E-W cross traffic, and started moving again at about 115.0. The signal turned green at 114.5 (red-amber on the median head from 111.5 to 114.0). labeling.md defines stop_line as a vehicle that stops past the line 'without going on into the junction', usually standing on the crossing. This SUV followed the trailer into the box and crept further in on red, so it was blocking the box, not overshooting the stop line. Other classes do not fit either. For red_light, the moment its front crossed the stop line cannot be seen: the SUV was hidden behind the trailer from about 64 to 86 s, and during that window the median three-lamp head was still green until 72 and amber until 75, even though the left two-lamp head, which the signal json uses, went red at 69.5. The 105.6-107.6 creep was inside the box, not over the stop line. For stopped_vehicle, the second stop lasted only about 7.5 s, and the start of the first stop (before 86 s) is hidden. The segment's start is also inconsistent with its own class, because the SUV had already been standing past the line since at least 86 s, not from 107.6. No class can be confirmed with observable boundaries, so I reject it. C3905.label: red_light
C3905.reason: The movement happened, but it does not meet the red_light definition closely enough to keep. The yellow-vest rider does wait at the head of the SB queue about 10 proxy px behind the stop line and starts creeping at about 33.0 s. In the 0.1 s crops (cross_b.jpg) the front wheel is on the line at 33.7 s and just past it at 33.8 s. By 34.4 s it is about 12 px past the line. At that moment the median head shows red and amber together, the "get ready" phase, not plain red (sig_med.jpg). Both camera-facing heads turn green at 34.5 s, so the rider crossed about 0.7 s before green. The SB queue was already starting to move during red+amber: the black SUV in the next lane creeps from about 34.0 s. This looks like a routine early start, not someone running the light. The SB heads face away from the camera, so a margin under 1 s is within the uncertainty of assuming the SB phase matches. The rider did not enter the junction on red. The labeller says it was on the north_sb zebra at 34.0-34.4 s, but that is wrong: at 34.4 s it is still about 20 px short of the stripes. It then slowed to let a westbound pedestrian in a light-blue shirt pass at 34.8-35.2 s and crossed the zebra only at about 35.4-36.6 s, on green. It left the frame at the bottom-right after 39.5 s (gone at 39.6 s). No other class fits. It never stood still past the line for 1 s, so it is not stop_line. The pedestrian had already passed its lane when it crossed the zebra, so it is not failure_to_yield. The start and end given are the boundaries it would have if kept. I am rejecting it as borderline.

C3905.label: failure_to_yield
C3905.reason: The sedan's movement is described correctly, but the situation does not meet the failure_to_yield definition. In the frames, the black sedan comes from the east and drives west along the lane just south of the pink islands. Its front reaches the east edge of the lower west zebra at 18.2 s, at about proxy (420,513), and its rear is past the west edge (about x 290) at 19.0 s. There was no conflict with the pedestrians. The group of three and the man walking a bicycle had come slowly down the zebra from the corner. At 18.2 to 19.0 s their feet were at about (210-290, 448-455). That puts them in the gap between the two lower islands, about level with the island tips and about 40 proxy px (roughly 5 to 6 stripes, about 3 m) north of the sedan's near side. They were not in its lane or stepping into it, and nobody took evasive action. Right after the sedan passed they stopped on the island line at about y 466. They stood there from about 21 s to 34 s and only crossed the southern lanes after the avenue phase turned green at 34.6 s. So they were waiting for their own phase while cross-street traffic had green. The same thing happened as white cars passed in the same lane at about 17.4 s and 29 s. Across the whole clip, no vehicle drove through the gap between the islands, so it works as a refuge and not as a lane next to the sedan's. The pedestrians were beyond the island line, not moving into the sedan's lane, and the sedan had right of way. I saw no swerve or braking, so near_miss does not apply either.

C3896.label: failure_to_yield
C3896.reason: The grey sedan's crossing is real and matches the description. Its front reaches the bottom edge of north_nb at about (718-727, 267) at 15.9-16.0 s, and its rear clears the top edge near (690, 247) at about 17.2-17.3 s. It fails the definition on the pedestrian side. I drew the NB lane lines from the median background (slope about 0.33, dividers L1/L2/L3 at y 238/218/196 at x 632) over the frames. The sedan's left wheels run along L1 the whole time, so it crossed in lane 2, next to the median lane. The girl in the white shirt walks east about 3-5 px north of the stripes' top edge (752,241 at 15.6 s, 764,239 at 15.9 s, 788,238 at 17.2 s), which puts her right on the L3 divider, between lanes 3 and 4. She is a full lane away from the sedan's lane and walking away from it, into lane 4. She is also at or past the middle of the zebra (about x 600-900). The dark pair is even further east (x 815-870). Lane 3, between them, was taken by the white convoy car directly ahead of the sedan. That car passed within about 1 m in front of the girl's feet (15.6-16.8 s) and screened her from the sedan. No pedestrian was in the sedan's path, and none was inside the lane next to it. The sedan passed well behind people who had already crossed its lane, which is the 'beyond a lane divider and not heading into the vehicle's lane' exclusion. The case is borderline at best, so I reject it. No other class fits: there was no evasive action, and the turn is a normal right turn. The real failure_to_yield here is that white car directly ahead. Its front was already on the zebra at 15.4 s (787,257), and its rear cleared the top edge at about 17.3 s, so this sedan's interval lies entirely inside it.
